summary: Preinstall dropper downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is obfuscator.io-style obfuscated (hex identifiers, shuffled string-array indirection) and, on `npm install`, downloads the Bun runtime v1.3.13 from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases into a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js` via `execFileSync`. math_init.js is a 727KB single-line Bun-bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header, rotated string-array obfuscation, hex-named identifiers) executed under the downloaded runtime, evading Node-based static analysis. Both setup.mjs and math_init.js sit at the tarball root and are not listed in package.json `files` (which declares only `dist` and `src`), indicating the payload was smuggled in outside the declared publish surface. The behavior is orthogonal to the package's declared purpose (an ESLint folder-schema plugin) and fires automatically at install time before any user action, matching the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern used to run attacker-controlled obfuscated code on install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
